title: EPIC Law Firm Group Releases Key Trends Driving Law Firm Malpractice Insurance Claims in Annual Survey — 15th annual Lawyers' Professional Liability Claims Survey
pub: Business Wire (EPIC Insurance Brokers & Consultants press release)
author: EPIC Law Firm Group · Eileen Garczynski

dom.t: Malpractice insurance: Reported AI claims remain hard to isolate

st.t: Malpractice insurance: Reported AI claims remain hard to isolate
st.an: EPIC’s release supports the synthesis by placing AI among insurer concerns without measuring AI-related claim incidence, while documenting broader malpractice-market pressures such as rising defense-counsel rates. Its insurer sample and absence of the full survey also reinforce the synthesis’s caution about treating these observations as claim counts or exposure-adjusted evidence.
qs: When asked about specific issues keeping them up at night, the surveyed insurers named cyber and attorney oversight as top areas of concern, as well as AI risks.

kp.k: Insurer survey identifies AI among malpractice risk concerns
kp.d: The 21 May 2025 press release reports findings from EPIC’s fifteenth annual Lawyers’ Professional Liability Claims survey, conducted by Eileen Garczynski. It polled 11 leading insurers that collectively insure more than 80% of the AM Law 100 and NLJ 250 firms. Respondents identified cyber, attorney oversight and AI risks as concerns. The release does not quantify AI-related claims or specify AI failure mechanisms; the document states that the full survey itself is not held.
qs: The survey examined key trends driving law firm malpractice exposures and claims by polling 11 leading lawyers’ professional liability insurance companies that, on a combined basis, provide insurance to more than 80% of the AM Law 100 and NLJ 250 firms.
When asked about specific issues keeping them up at night, the surveyed insurers named cyber and attorney oversight as top areas of concern, as well as AI risks.

kp.k: Flexible working and mergers may weaken attorney oversight
kp.d: Garczynski suggests that flexible work schedules and merger growth may blur supervisory responsibilities for remote attorneys, new joiners and departing lawyers, creating unchecked risks and accountability gaps. This is her qualified explanation of post-Covid oversight concerns, not a quantified survey finding or an effect attributed to AI.
qs: As firms increase flexible work schedules and experience more merger growth the past several years, there is growing concern that some law firms may have blurred the lines of oversight for attorneys working from home, new joiners, and even those transitioning out of the firm,
This post-Covid phenomena may be leading to unchecked risks and lapses in accountability.

kp.k: Malpractice defense counsel rates rose across most surveyed insurers
kp.d: Ten of the 11 insurers reported increases in defense counsel rates last year: three reported increases of 5% to 10%, and seven reported increases of 2% to 5%. Garczynski attributes law firm rates and malpractice defense costs to growing legal-services demand, competition for talent and operational costs. The release does not attribute these increases to AI.
qs: Ten of the 11 insurers surveyed reported that the rates they pay defense counsel increased last year.
Among them, three saw rates increase by 5% to 10%, and seven noted increases of 2% to 5%.
The growing demand for legal services, the pressure to hire top talent, and the necessity to cover operational costs are all drivers of the law firm rates and legal malpractice claim defense costs,

kp.k: Claims concentrate in three practice areas
kp.d: Surveyed insurers identified Trust & Estate, Business Transactions and Corporate & Securities as the three main practice areas generating claims. The release also reports a growing percentage of malpractice claims associated with insurance defense work, without providing numerical shares or linking these practice-area patterns to AI.
qs: Polled insurers named Trust & Estate, Business Transactions and Corporate & Securities as the three main practice areas generating claims.
Insurance defense work is also seeing a growing percentage of legal malpractice claims.

kp.k: Garczynski urges vigilance against costly professional errors
kp.d: Against the reported backdrop of malpractice litigation and rising costs, Garczynski recommends continued firm vigilance to preserve credibility and prevent common errors that can trigger expensive disputes. The recommendation is general rather than an AI-specific verification or governance protocol.
qs: Firms must remain hypervigilant to maintain their credibility and avoid the common errors that can prompt costly legal disputes.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: EPIC reports that surveyed legal malpractice insurers identify AI risks as a concern, alongside cyber risks and attorney oversight.
pts.d: The press release reporting Eileen Garczynski’s survey makes a limited claim about insurers’ expressed concerns. It does not identify particular AI-related errors, establish that AI has caused malpractice claims, or predict changes in legal work, staffing, pricing or insurance premiums. The reported increases in defense costs and concerns about remote-work oversight are not explicitly attributed to AI.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered is a qualitative summary of responses to a survey of 11 lawyers’ professional liability insurers.
pts.d: EPIC states that the participating insurers collectively cover more than 80% of AM Law 100 and NLJ 250 firms. The release does not report how many respondents mentioned AI, quantify AI-related claims or losses, or provide examples of AI-related incidents. Only the press release is supplied; the full survey is not available in the provided document.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: AI risk is presented as a current concern in the 2025 annual survey announcement, not as a forecast.
pts.d: The release is dated 21 May 2025. No AI-specific observation period, future horizon, adoption threshold or other condition is stated. The phrase “last year” in the defense-cost findings should not be treated as the observation period for the AI concern.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The reported concern directly concerns legal malpractice insurers and, by implication, the law firms whose professional liability they insure.
pts.d: The survey is framed around U.S. law firm malpractice exposures, with substantial insurer coverage of AM Law 100 and NLJ 250 firms. It does not specify which firm sizes, practice areas, lawyer roles or clients face AI-related risks, or describe any resulting changes to coverage, underwriting or service delivery.
